# NPM Improved v1.6.3 — NPMX sync visibility and clean navigation

## NPMX synchronization status correctness
- The primary now derives its most recent successful synchronization from authenticated secondary success heartbeats. A pairing or check-in alone does not count as a successful configuration snapshot.
- Primary status distinguishes *latest completed secondary sync* from *latest secondary check-in*.
- Secondary status distinguishes the actual last successful snapshot application from its last attempted pull and any reported error.
- The peers table separates Last seen from Last successful sync. Previously these dates could be displayed as if interchangeable.
- The "In sync" badge no longer appears just because NPMX is enabled. The UI distinguishes disabled, awaiting first completed sync, synchronization error, and successful history.
- A secondary now checks the HTTP status of its post-apply heartbeat and reports any heartbeat delivery failure without falsely treating the successfully applied snapshot as failed. Subsequent periodic synchronization retries reporting.
- CI verifies that a secondary's successful pull timestamp is present on both peers following the authenticated heartbeat.
- Version mismatch safety checks, read-only secondary rules, transactional snapshot rollback and scheduled synchronization are unchanged.

## Navigation
- Remove unintended underlined text from the permanent side navigation, Analytics section navigation, header menus and shared nav-link components, including hover, focus, visited and active states.
- Preserve focus-visible outlines for keyboard accessibility and preserve the designed active-page visual indicators.
- Ordinary content hyperlinks remain unaffected.

## Availability and rollout
- This release follows v1.6.2, which addresses cross-node session validation, expiry routing, node identity, and updater network resilience.
- Upgrade both NPMX nodes sequentially and verify identical versions before expecting configuration snapshots to resume. NPMX intentionally refuses snapshot application across incompatible application versions.
- If the secondary still shows no completed sync, inspect its Last pull attempt and Last error in Settings > Instance Synchronization, then run Sync now from the secondary node's management URL to get the precise failure.
